brief: Security fix SEC-5 (tighten-only). redact.scrub_text (jarvis/v2/redact.py) redacts only the header and footer lines of a PEM, OpenSSH or PGP private key, so the key body goes out unredacted on every surface scrub_text feeds (Discord mirror and reporter, diff review, chat git, providers, subagents, the daemon). Make it redact the whole private-key block as a single [redacted], for RSA, OPENSSH, EC, ENCRYPTED (PKCS#8 and legacy Proc-Type/DEK-Info), PGP and plain PKCS#8 keys, in these shapes: a complete block; a block with no footer (through the end of the text); a footer with no header (the key-material lines directly above it, and no more; a line of key material is a run of base64, a PGP checksum line '=' plus 4 characters, or a Proc-Type: / DEK-Info: line, and the walk upward stops at the first other line, such as a blank line or one containing words; a footer preceded by a line of words changes nothing above it). Two blocks in one text stay two blocks. Public keys, certificates and text with no private-key header or footer come out byte for byte as they do today, and nothing the current scrub hides may become visible (including a token-character run glued to a header). Matching must stay fast: 1 MiB adversarial inputs finish within a CPU bound. Interface the tests call directly: redact.private_key_blocks(text) -> str, which keeps CR characters (scrub_text itself normalises line endings). Test key bodies are random seeded base64, never real keys.
